value_stream.name: Customer Pickup Truck & Cargo Van Rental (Self-Haul) Operations

fields.Trigger: Telematics crash/harsh-event alert (W4749); customer call-in of accident/damage/breakdown; police/third-party report

workflows.name: Rental Vehicle Accident, Damage & Roadside Event Response

Automation Opportunity: - - System auto-alert of telematics crash detection with location routed to dispatcher and Insurance
- System auto-capture of mobile damage-estimate photos at scene
- System auto-assign of substitute vehicle from available fleet
Controls: - CTL-718 (ensure controlled execution — Incident, Damage, Compliance & Rental Analytics (PA-162.3).)
- CTL-718: serious events escalated to Safety/Legal/Insurance immediately; scene evidence (telematics + photos + police report) captured before vehicle moves
Cross-references: - links to VS-24 (safety), VS-26 (insurance), VS-23 (LP), VS-100/VS-88 (legal/records), W4749 (telematics), W4750 (substitute vehicle), W4762 (claim)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Injury-liability risk**: An accident causing bodily injury → catastrophic liability; mitigated by immediate emergency/Safety/Legal/Insurance escalation and the umbrella cover (W4748)
- **Evidence-loss risk**: Missing scene evidence → failed insurance/subrogation recovery (W4762); mitigated by the telematics snapshot + photo protocol
- **Customer-stranding risk**: A stranded customer with no substitute vehicle → service failure; mitigated by substitute-vehicle provisioning
System Touchpoints: - Telematics event alert (W4749); insurance claim (VS-26); maintenance/workshop (W4750/VS-31); safety incident (VS-24); legal/records (VS-100/VS-88)
Time Estimate: - ~per event 2–8 hrs active response + documentation; ~recovery absorbed in W4762

steps.activity: Triage the event on telematics + customer call: severity, location, injuries, third-party involvement, vehicle drivability; if injury/serious → emergency services + notify Safety/LP (VS-24) + Legal (VS-100) + Insurance (VS-26) immediately; capture the customer's statement and photos at scene

Coordinate roadside response: recovery/tow to nearest approved workshop (VS-31/W4750), substitute vehicle for the stranded customer (W4750) if the rental continues, and liaison with police for the incident report (required for insurance W4762 and any third-party claim)

Document the event end-to-end (telematics snapshot, photos, police report, statements, workshop damage estimate) into the claim file (W4762); preserve evidence per Legal/records (VS-88/VS-100); if the customer was at-fault and LDW declined, trigger deductible recovery (W4756/W4762); if a third party was at-fault, prepare subrogation (W4762)

fields.Trigger: Damage event (W4761); return-damage charge (W4759); total loss
fields.Volume: ~10–35 claims/month, per the W4761 event rate (~1–3% of ~800–1,200 rentals/month)

workflows.name: Damage Recovery, Insurance Claim, Deductible Settlement & Subrogation

Automation Opportunity: - Claim file auto-assembly from telematics/agreement/workshop; deductible auto-capture-from-deposit; loss-ratio dashboard feeding W4748 re-pricing
Controls: - CTL-718 (ensure controlled execution — Incident, Damage, Compliance & Rental Analytics (PA-162.3).)
- CTL-718: deductible collected per LDW election; insurer claim filed with full evidence; subrogation pursued for at-fault third parties; finance-recon
Cross-references: - links to VS-26 (insurance/claims), VS-100 (legal/subrogation), VS-31 (workshop), VS-17 (GL), W4748 (LDW/deductible), W4756 (deposit), W4759 (return damage), W4761 (event), W4752 (total loss)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unrecovered-deductible risk**: Customer disputes or insufficient deposit → fleet absorbs; mitigated by the deposit level = deductible (W4748/W4756) and clear terms
- **Subrogation-failure risk**: At-fault third party not pursued → loss; mitigated by the Legal subrogation step
- **Claim-leakage risk**: Overstated estimates or duplicate recovery; mitigated by workshop estimate validation and finance recon
System Touchpoints: - Insurance claims (VS-26 PA-26.3 W862/W1565); rental billing/deposit (W4756/W4760); GL (VS-17); legal (VS-100); workshop (VS-31)
Time Estimate: - ~per claim 1–6 weeks to settle depending on complexity

steps.activity: Open the claim with the insurer (CTPL for third-party bodily/property; comprehensive for own-damage/theft per W4748); submit the evidence file (W4761), workshop estimate (VS-31), and the agreement/LDW election (W4755/W4757); track to settlement

Settle the customer-deductible: if LDW taken and terms met → no customer charge; if LDW declined/at-fault → capture the deductible from the deposit (W4756/W4759) or invoice the customer; reconcile deductible vs repair cost vs insurer settlement; if total-loss, retire the vehicle (W4752) and settle actual-cash-value

Where a third party is at-fault, pursue subrogation/recovery via Legal (VS-100) against the third party/their insurer; manage unrecovered balances; feed claim outcomes to the loss-experience re-pricing (W4748) and analytics (W4768)

fields.Trigger: Vehicle past scheduled return with no check-in; geofence breach alert (W4749); do-not-rent/fraud signal (VS-125)

workflows.name: Vehicle Non-Return, Theft & Fraud Recovery (Geofence-Breach Response)

Automation Opportunity: - Telematics auto-non-return-alert + GPS recovery workflow; do-not-rent auto-screen (W4754); fraud-pattern detection (VS-125)
Controls: - CTL-718 (ensure controlled execution — Incident, Damage, Compliance & Rental Analytics (PA-162.3).)
- CTL-718: non-return escalated within grace period; police-led recovery; offender watch-listed; insurance/legal recovery pursued
Cross-references: - links to VS-23 (LP), VS-125 (fraud), VS-159 (security/law-enforcement pattern), VS-26 (theft insurance), VS-100 (legal), W4749 (telematics/GPS), W4754 (do-not-rent), W4756 (deposit), W4752 (write-off)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Asset-loss risk**: A vehicle not recovered → ~PHP 1.5–3M asset write-off per pickup/van; mitigated by telematics + police recovery + insurance theft cover
- **Fraud-pattern risk**: Organized rental-fraud rings; mitigated by do-not-rent screen (W4754) + VS-125 fraud intelligence sharing
- **Recovery-safety risk**: Confronting a thief; mitigated by police-led recovery (never self-help)
System Touchpoints: - Telematics GPS recovery (W4749); LP/investigation (VS-23); police coordination (VS-159 pattern); insurance theft claim (VS-26/W4748); legal (VS-100); do-not-rent list (W4754)
Time Estimate: - ~per event hours-to-days for recovery; ~legal recovery weeks-months

steps.activity: Detect non-return/geofence-breach from telematics (W4749) at the grace-period expiry; attempt customer contact (per agreement W4755); if no response or confirmed unauthorized use → escalate to LP (VS-23), begin recovery, and notify Insurance (theft claim W4748) and Legal (VS-100)

Use telematics GPS to locate and recover the vehicle with police assistance (VS-23 coordinates law-enforcement per VS-159 W4694 pattern); file a police report (theft/estafa under the Revised Penal Code / RA 10951); recover via the deposit (W4756) and pursue the customer legally for unpaid rental, damage, and costs

Add the offender to the do-not-rent watch-list (W4754); recover via insurance if unrecovered (theft claim W4748/W4762); retire the vehicle from the register if not recovered (W4752); feed the event to fraud analytics (VS-125) and the do-not-rent screen

fields.Trigger: Citation/toll notice received by BuildRight (registered owner) for a vehicle during a customer's rental
fields.Volume: ~notices benchmarked ~1–5% of rentals (speeding, no-contact-apprehension, parking, toll)

workflows.name: Traffic Violation, Citation & Toll Violation Handling (Customer Recharge)

Automation Opportunity: - Notice→rental-record auto-match (telematics date/time + plate + agreement); auto-recharge to deposit/billing; toll/NCAP batch reconciliation; repeat-offender auto-watchlist
Controls: - CTL-718 (ensure controlled execution — Incident, Damage, Compliance & Rental Analytics (PA-162.3).)
- CTL-718: notices matched to rental within SLA; uncontested paid timely (owner-liability); customer recharged per agreement; repeat offenders watchlisted
Cross-references: - links to VS-22 (compliance), VS-100 (legal), VS-79 (BIR rental revenue), W4747 (owner-liability), W4749 (telematics matching), W4754 (do-not-rent), W4755/W4756/W4760 (recharge)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Owner-liability risk**: As registered owner, BuildRight is liable for unpaid citations → default judgment/registration hold (W4747); mitigated by timely payment + customer recharge
- **Unrecovered-recharge risk**: Customer disputes/absconds → BuildRight absorbs the fine; mitigated by deposit-capture and agreement terms
- **False-apprehension risk**: Paying a notice the customer didn't incur, or recharging the wrong customer; mitigated by telematics verification before recharge
System Touchpoints: - Rental/telematics matching (W4749/W4755); billing/deposit (W4756/W4760); toll/NCAP operator integration; legal/compliance (VS-100/VS-22)
Time Estimate: - ~per notice 15–45 min; ~uncontested penalties paid within the LGU/LTO SLA

steps.activity: Receive the citation/toll notice addressed to BuildRight (registered owner); match the notice date/time + plate to the rental record (telematics W4749 + agreement W4755) to identify the customer who was driving; verify via telematics that the vehicle was on-rent to that customer at the time

Recharge the penalty + an administrative fee to the customer per the agreement (W4755): capture from the deposit (W4756) or invoice/bill the customer (W4760); contest the notice if telematics proves the vehicle was elsewhere (false-apprehension defense); pay the uncontested penalty timely to avoid BuildRight liability (registered-owner default)

Manage the no-contact-apprehension program (MMDA/LTO NCAP) and toll (RFID) reconciliation; report repeat-offender customers to the do-not-rent list (W4754); track notice volume as a driver-behavior KPI (links W4768)

fields.Trigger: Customer disputes a rental charge (W4760), damage/deductible (W4759/W4762), fuel/cleaning/late fee, or files a complaint/chargeback (VS-80/VS-13/W469)

Automation Opportunity: - Evidence-pack auto-assembly; chargeback-representment workflow (links VS-80); root-cause tagging → VS-133
Controls: - CTL-718 (ensure controlled execution — Incident, Damage, Compliance & Rental Analytics (PA-162.3).)
- CTL-718: disputes resolved with evidence; chargebacks represented within window; DTI escalations handled per W469; outcomes feed improvement
Cross-references: - links to VS-13 (CX/complaint), VS-80 (chargeback W537/W267), W469 (DTI escalation), VS-100 (legal), VS-133 (improvement), W4755/W4758/W4759/W4760 (evidence sources), W4768 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lost-chargeback risk**: Weak evidence → lost representment + revenue loss; mitigated by the telematics+photoset+agreement evidence pack
- **Reputational risk**: A viral rental-dispute complaint; mitigated by first-contact resolution + DTI-compliant handling (W469)
- **Recurring-root-cause risk**: Same dispute repeating (e.g., unclear fuel policy); mitigated by feeding to VS-133 improvement
System Touchpoints: - Rental/billing records; telematics/photoset evidence (W4749/W4758/W4759); chargeback system (VS-80); CX/complaint (VS-13); DTI escalation (VS-22/W469); legal (VS-100)
Time Estimate: - ~per case 20 min–2 hrs; ~chargeback within scheme window

steps.activity: Triage the dispute: rental charge, damage/deductible (W4759/W4762), fuel/cleaning/late, LDW, or service; pull the evidence (telematics W4749, photosets W4758/W4759, agreement W4755, billing W4760); attempt first-contact resolution where the evidence supports the customer

For chargebacks (VS-80/card-scheme) or formal complaints (VS-13/W469 DTI): assemble the representment evidence pack (signed agreement + telematics + photoset + billing) and submit within the scheme's window (links VS-80 W537/W267 chargeback representment pattern); coordinate with Legal (VS-100) for escalated claims

Resolve and close: refund/credit where due, uphold where justified, record the outcome and root cause; feed repeat issues to process/quality improvement (VS-133) and to analytics (W4768); manage DTI Consumer Act (RA 7394) escalations (W469)

fields.Trigger: Annual compliance review; regulatory change; audit (VS-21/VS-22); incident (W4761)
fields.Volume: 1 compliance program across the rental fleet/operations

workflows.name: Rental Regulatory Compliance — LTO/LTFRB, DOLE Driver Fitness, Consumer Act

Automation Opportunity: - Compliance-obligation calendar; regulator-interaction log; agreement/pricing transparency audit checklist
Controls: - CTL-718 (ensure controlled execution — Incident, Damage, Compliance & Rental Analytics (PA-162.3).)
- CTL-718: rental classified correctly (self-drive, not for-hire freight); agreement/pricing/LDW/consent Legally reviewed annually; assured by Internal Audit
Cross-references: - links to VS-22 (compliance), VS-100 (legal), VS-21 (audit), VS-79 (BIR), W469 (DTI), VS-88 (records), W4747/W4748/W4755/W4757 (regulated artifacts)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Liability-structure risk**: Misclassifying the rental (e.g., as for-hire freight) → wrong regulatory regime + LTFRB exposure; mitigated by the legal classification
- **Consumer-Act risk**: Unclear pricing/terms → DTI complaint (W469) + penalty; mitigated by transparent disclosure

- **Officer-liability risk**: Registered-owner defaults (unpaid citations/unregistered release) → officer personal liability; mitigated by the release gate (W4758/W4759) and timely citation handling (W4764)
System Touchpoints: - Compliance/legal (VS-22/VS-100); records (VS-88); audit (VS-21); BIR (VS-79); DTI escalation (W469)

steps.activity: Maintain the regulatory map for self-haul vehicle rental: LTO motor-vehicle registration (W4747) + CTPL mandate (RA 4136, W4748); the BuildRight-vs-customer liability structure under the Civil Code + Land Transportation rules; Consumer Act (RA 7394) on rental-disclosure, pricing transparency, and unfair-contract terms (links W469); BIR VAT/e-invoicing on rental revenue (VS-79 W4760); and the distinction from LTFRB cargo-freight licensing (VS-06) — a customer self-drive rental is not a for-hire/freight operation

Ensure the rental agreement (W4755), pricing disclosure (W4745/W4760), LDW language (W4757), and telematics consent (W4755/W4767) comply with consumer-protection and contract standards; review annually with Legal; assure via Internal Audit (VS-21 W344 trade-promo/spend or W339 regulatory audit pattern)

Manage regulator interactions (LTO registration audits, DTI consumer complaints W469, BIR rental-revenue scrutiny VS-79), incident regulatory reporting (W4761), and officer personal-liability awareness (registered-owner liability); maintain the records (VS-88)

fields.Trigger: Rental launch (privacy-by-design); DSAR/erasure request; periodic privacy review (VS-91)
fields.Volume: Every rental (~800–1,200/month) collects license image + selfie + telematics + billing PII; ~10–20 DSARs/year

workflows.name: Rental Data Privacy — License/Image/Telematics Data Governance & DSAR

Automation Opportunity: - Consent registry auto-update; DSAR workflow (links VS-91.2 W271); retention-auto-purge; breach playbook (VS-91)
Controls: - CTL-718 (ensure controlled execution — Incident, Damage, Compliance & Rental Analytics (PA-162.3).)
- CTL-718: data minimized & classified; telematics consent at rental (W4755); secured (VS-27.3); retention per VS-88 then purge; DSAR handled per VS-91.2
Cross-references: - links to VS-91/VS-91.2 (privacy/DPIA/DSAR W271/W3052), VS-27.3 (cyber), VS-88 (records), VS-100.3 (legal), W4754 (license data), W4749 (telematics), W4755 (consent)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-collection risk**: Collecting more PII/telematics than needed → RA 10173 exposure; mitigated by data minimization
- **DSAR-conflict risk**: Erasure request vs BIR 10-yr retention → legal tension; mitigated by documented retention overrides
- **Telematics-breach risk**: Compromised driving data → privacy harm; mitigated by VS-27.3 security + DPIA
System Touchpoints: - Privacy/consent registry (VS-91.2); DPIA (VS-91.2 W3052); cyber (VS-27.3); records/retention (VS-88); DSAR workflow (VS-91.2 W271)
Time Estimate: - ~DPIA 2–4 weeks at launch; ~DSAR per SLA; ~annual review absorbed

steps.activity: Govern the personal data the rental program collects: driver-license image + ID selfie (W4754), telematics driving data (W4749), billing/payment data (W4760), and dispute/citation data (W4764/W4765) — classify per VS-91, minimize collection, secure storage (VS-27.3), retention aligned to BIR/legal need (10-yr VS-88 per TRAIN/NIRC Sec. 235) and then purge

Handle Data Subject Access Requests (DSAR) per RA 10173 (VS-91.2 W271): access, correction, erasure (where legally permissible — note BIR retention conflicts), and objection; manage telematics-consent withdrawal and the do-not-rent list data minimization; coordinate with the DPO

Run the breach-response path if rental PII/telematics is compromised (VS-91 breach notification, NPC 72-hour); DPIA for high-risk processing (telematics + biometric selfie); annual privacy review with the DPO and Cyber (VS-27.3)

fields.Trigger: Monthly/quarterly performance review; annual capex & pricing case (W4745); continuous monitoring

workflows.name: Rental Revenue, Utilization, Attach-Uplift & Fleet-Performance Analytics

Automation Opportunity: - Rental-P&L auto-dashboard; attach-uplift measurement (POS bulky-line × rental-availability); loss/utilization benchmarking; auto-feed to W4745/W4751/W4752
Controls: - CTL-718 (ensure controlled execution — Incident, Damage, Compliance & Rental Analytics (PA-162.3).)
- CTL-718: rental P&L + attach-uplift + utilization + loss-rate reported monthly; outcomes feed sizing/pricing/rebalancing/replacement
Cross-references: - links to VS-28 (analytics), VS-17.4 (FP&A), VS-133 (improvement), W4745/W4751/W4752 (sizing/rebalancing/replacement), W4749/W4757/W4761–W4765 (performance inputs)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Strategic-invisibility risk**: If attach-uplift isn't measured, the program looks like a cost center and gets cut; mitigated by the attach-uplift KPI
- **Loss-ratio-creep risk**: Rising claims/citations eroding margin; mitigated by loss-rate monitoring and re-pricing (W4748)
- **Utilization-blindspot risk**: Idle vehicles at some stores while others turn customers away; mitigated by the rebalancing KPI (W4751)
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (VS-28); rental platform data (new); telematics (W4749); finance FP&A (VS-17.4); merchandising/POS attach data (VS-08/VS-01); LP/claims (VS-23/VS-26)

steps.activity: Track the rental P&L and unit economics: rental revenue, fuel recovery, LDW income, attach-uplift (incremental large-item basket completed because a vehicle was available), direct costs (depreciation, insurance, maintenance, fuel, telematics, staffing), claim losses (W4762), and net contribution per vehicle/store/region

Track fleet performance: utilization rate, turn-down (lost-rental) rate, downtime (W4750), incident/loss rate (W4761/W4762), non-return rate (W4763), citation rate (W4764), dispute/chargeback rate (W4765), and LDW take-rate/loss-ratio (W4757/W4748); benchmark across stores and identify outliers

Report to leadership quarterly with the attach-uplift/ROI story (the strategic reason the fleet exists), feed the annual fleet-sizing & pricing case (W4745) and rebalancing (W4751) and replacement cycle (W4752); drive continuous improvement (VS-133) on loss/utilization drivers
